scope: rfigc.py selected lines 75-115,311-360,390-505,525-600; test_rfigc.py read whole. Not whole rfigc review.

findings.detail: The reviewed rfigc integrity/recovery path uses its own generate_hashes, streaming full MD5 and SHA1 in one 65536-byte pass. It does not call the shortened Hasher facade. v1 short-key collision result must not be attributed to this path.

Hashes are computed through one file handle, then structure and metadata through reopened path/os.stat without a before/after identity/content stamp. A replacement can combine digests of an earlier file with metadata of a later file. No cancellation parameter or work budget.

Recovery stores md5 and sha1 maps to a single row ID. Multiple original paths with identical content overwrite earlier destinations, so restoring all original names is not represented. No full-byte equality confirmation against a trusted original.
Remove-update closes a .rem file, then explicitly removes old database before renaming replacement. Rename failure after deletion leaves old database unavailable. No atomic replace/fsync transaction.

Remove-update skips rows for nonselected paths with continue before writing them into replacement. Single-file use can therefore omit unrelated database rows; this is a source-level finding, not an executed reproduction.
Update-append skips existing paths regardless of changed content. It adds new paths rather than refreshing existing integrity observations; consumers must not treat append as revalidation.

Six original test functions cover file/directory generation, tamper reporting, recovery, update and known hash vectors. partial_eq uses substring membership rather than exact row multiset equality, so extra/duplicate output rows can escape assertions. No upstream tests run.
